fields.meta_title: Quote Form Builder for Service Businesses | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a quote form that asks what sets the price, prices standard jobs on screen and emails the quote back with an expiry date. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Quote Form That Collects What You Need to Price the Job
fields.hero_description: Describe your services and how you price them. Emergent builds the quote form, works out the number for standard jobs and saves every request to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Quote Form Has to Get Right
fields.features_subheading: Six parts turn a stranger's request into a priced job your team can schedule.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that set the price

Ask only what changes the number: square footage, bedrooms, quantity, or material. Emergent adds a follow-up field when an answer needs one, like floor and elevator for a move.
fields.feature_2:
Instant figures for standard jobs

Write your rates into the prompt, and the form applies them as the customer types. Requests that fall outside your rules skip the instant figure and go to a person for review.
fields.feature_3:
Photo and drawing uploads

Let customers attach photos of the site or a part drawing with the request. Files sit next to the answers in the record, and the estimator sees them before anyone drives out.
fields.feature_4:
Requests routed by job size

Send large or unusual requests to your senior estimator and the rest to a shared queue. Alerts arrive in Slack or by email with a link to the full request and its files.
fields.feature_5:
Priced quotes emailed back

Turn a priced request into an emailed quote with line items, a quote number and an expiry date. A reminder goes out if the client has not replied, and lapsed quotes are marked.
fields.feature_6:
Source code you can take with you

Publish the form on your own domain or embed it on your current site. Export the full source to GitHub on paid plans when a developer wants your pricing rules to sync with the CRM.

fields.usecase_heading: Quote Forms at Work in Four Trades
fields.tab_content_1:
Two-bedroom moves priced while the customer waits

Tidewater Moving asks for the move date, the ZIP codes, bedrooms and stairs at each end. A two-bedroom move starts at $900, and each flight without an elevator adds $120. Two flights put this one at $1,140 on screen. Homes with four or more bedrooms book a video walkthrough instead.
fields.tab_content_2:
Yard photos land in Slack ahead of each site visit

Homeowners pick the job at Greenway Landscaping, like a patio or sod, enter the yard size and upload up to 5 photos. Each request posts to the #estimates channel in Slack with the photos attached. The estimator books the visit from that message, already knowing the 1,800 square feet of lawn sits on a slope.
fields.tab_content_3:
A part drawing priced at 500 and 1,000 pieces

Purchasing at Kestrel Pumps uploads a PDF drawing of a bracket, picks the material and asks for prices at 500 and 1,000 pieces. The estimator at Ridgeline Machine enters a unit price for each: $11.80 and $9.60. Kestrel gets one email with both totals, $5,900 and $9,600, on a quote valid for 30 days.
fields.tab_content_4:
Unanswered quotes get a reminder before they lapse

Brightwell Cleaning quotes most offices on a monthly plan. Marlow Dental's 6,000-square-foot office gets 12 visits at $130, or $1,560 a month. If the office manager has not replied by day 10, a reminder email goes out with the quote attached. On day 14 the quote is marked expired and leaves the open list.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Quote Form
fields.howto_description: Settle your pricing rules before you write the prompt.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start from your own price sheet
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for what changes the number
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose the jobs you price on screen
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for photos where they save a trip
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull up the rates you already quote by phone: a base price per job size and the extras that move it. Every number on that sheet becomes a rule the form applies, and anything without a rule goes to a person.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Every question on the form should move the price or the schedule. For a move, that means bedrooms and stairs. For office cleaning, it means square feet and visits per week. Drop anything your estimator would never read.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Price the jobs you can price without seeing them, and send the rest to a person. A two-bedroom apartment is predictable. A four-bedroom house with a piano is not, and a guessed number there costs you the job or the margin.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Turn on uploads for work a picture explains, like a sloped yard or a part drawing. Set a limit, such as 5 files, and tell customers which angles you need. A good photo can replace the first site visit.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your rates and rules into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the form and a requests table behind it, with your pricing applied as customers type. Change a rate or add a question later by asking in the same chat.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set an expiry and a follow-up
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick how long a quote stays valid; 30 days is common for standard work. Add a reminder email a few days before it lapses, and mark expired quotes so your open list shows only the deals still in play.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form as a customer would, with a photo attached. Check the figure on screen against your price sheet. Then open the requests table and confirm every answer landed in the right column before you share the link.

claims_to_source: A quote is a firm price for a defined scope that the client can accept, while an estimate is an approximate figure that can change
A quote usually carries a quote number, issue and expiry dates, the business and client details, line items with quantities and prices, taxes and terms
A request for quotation (RFQ) asks suppliers to price a clearly defined product with set specifications and quantities
A quote should state how long it stays valid, and 30 days is a common validity period
